autoBids.notes: The 5 highest-ranked conference champions got bids. In practice this always included at least one G5 champion. The original 6+6 model (approved 2022-09-02) changed to 5+7 in 2024 after the Pac-12 collapsed.

formats.notreDameRule: No special access. Notre Dame earned an at-large bid.
formats.seeding: Top 4 seeds and first-round byes went to the four highest-ranked conference champions (Oregon, Georgia, Boise State, Arizona State).
formats.notes: First 12-team CFP. Ohio State beat Notre Dame 34-23. The Sugar Bowl quarterfinal moved to Jan 2 after the New Orleans attack. Bowl tie-ins (Rose: Big Ten, Sugar: SEC, etc.) still decided which bowls the top-4 champions went to.

autoBids.notes: Same access rule as 2024-25. On 2025-05-22 the Management Committee switched to straight seeding, so the top 4 ranked teams get byes whether or not they won their conference.

formats.seeding: Straight seeding by committee ranking. Top 4 teams get byes.
formats.note: Champion and runner-up are from researcher knowledge and were not re-verified this session. Search snippets confirm Miami beat Ole Miss in a semifinal and that no SEC team reached the title game.
formats.notes: The SEC earned close to $40M in CFP money despite having no team in the final. Miami kept all of its CFP money, $14M+ (the ACC passes 100% through to schools).

formats.model: 5+7 (P4 champions + top G6 team), straight seeding

autoBids.notes: This is the default from the 2024 MOU, which applied because the SEC and Big Ten did not agree on expansion by the 2026-01-23 deadline. The ACC, Big 12, Big Ten and SEC champions get automatic bids regardless of ranking. One more bid goes to the highest-ranked team from the Group of Six (American, CUSA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12, Sun Belt). NCAA.com and OutKick report that this team does not have to be a conference champion. Some outlets describe it as the top-ranked G6 champion.

formats.notreDameRule: Notre Dame is guaranteed a bid, but not a seed, if it finishes in the committee's top 12 (2026 MOU term). It still takes an at-large slot.
formats.seeding: Straight seeding. The top 4 ranked teams get byes. Seeds 1, 2 and 3 pick their quarterfinal bowl in that order, and the No. 1 seed also picks its semifinal path. Seed 4 gets the remaining bowl. All conference tie-ins to the Rose, Sugar and Orange bowls are gone.
formats.broadcast: ESPN family, plus 5 games sublicensed to TNT Sports: the two first-round games on 2026-12-19 (3:30 and 7:30 pm ET on TNT, truTV and HBO Max) and more. Sources conflict on whether TNT has the Orange Bowl semifinal; the official schedule lists the Sugar semifinal on ABC/ESPN.
formats.notes: Season in progress on 2026-11-25. This is the last 12-team season and the last season with Power 4 conference championship games.

formats.decidedBy: CFP Management Committee (10 FBS commissioners + Notre Dame AD), unanimous, with the presidents' Board of Managers' sign-off. This came well ahead of the 2026-12-01 deadline for a 2027 format.

autoBids.notes: ACC, Big 12, Big Ten and SEC champions, plus the highest-ranked G6 team. There is still only one guaranteed G6 slot. With no Power 4 title games, each P4 conference names its champion from regular-season standings and tiebreakers.

formats.notreDameRule: Competes for at-large bids. Reporting on the 24-team deal did not mention a separate Notre Dame guarantee beyond the at-large pool.
formats.seeding: Committee ranks the field. Seeds 1-8 get first-round byes and host second-round games on campus. Seeds 9-16 host seeds 17-24 in the first round on campus.

firstRound.dates: first full week of December 2027 (exact dates TBA)

formats.conferenceChampionshipGames: The Power 4 (SEC, Big Ten, ACC, Big 12) title games are eliminated from 2027. Rights holders get rebates: about $140M a year from the SEC, ACC and Big 12 to ESPN, and a reported ~$50M a year from the Big Ten to Fox. G6 title games are undecided (each league chooses).
formats.regularSeasonCalendar: Two open weeks are built into the regular season. Army-Navy moves to the first weekend of December, the old championship weekend (per Yahoo).
formats.notes: This matches the brief's 24-team claim (19 at-large + P4 champions + top G6) and its 5-year ~$1.7B ESPN deal, which comes on top of the existing $7.8B contract. The bracket also adds Power 4 teams to lower bowls: reporting describes teams that miss the CFP filling the remaining bowls (e.g., Music City, Texas).

championshipSites.note: Reported, not officially confirmed in the sources found.

formats.notes: The format is locked through the 2031-32 season, when both the base ESPN deal and the expansion deal end. The Rose Bowl will not host a semifinal in 2028-31; it keeps its Jan 1 slot.

expansionDebate.event: Board of Managers approves a 12-team 6+6 format, originally for 2026.
12-team start moved up to the 2024 season.

FBS conferences and Notre Dame agree to a 6-year CFP deal for 2026-31 with a revenue split weighted toward the SEC and Big Ten. ESPN agrees to a $7.8B, 6-year extension. A memorandum of understanding gives the SEC and Big Ten control of the format from 2026.
Format changes from 6+6 to 5+7 after the Pac-12's collapse.

16-team models are debated. The 4-4-2-2-1(+3 at-large) model, backed by the Big Ten and initially the SEC, gives the Big Ten and SEC 4 automatic bids each, the ACC and Big 12 2 each, and the G6 1. The 5+11 model is backed by the ACC and Big 12. SEC coaches push back on the 4-4 model.

The SEC moves to 5+11. The Big Ten pivots to a 24-team field with multiple automatic bids per conference. Big Ten ADs say they would accept 5+11 only if the SEC plays 9 conference games. The Big Ten floats a 16-team stopgap tied to a commitment to go to 24 later.

Deadline passes with the Big Ten and SEC deadlocked. The 2026 default applies: 12 teams, P4 champions + top G6, straight seeding, and a Notre Dame top-12 guarantee. The next deadline (for 2027) is set for 2026-12-01.
CFP reaches a 'handshake agreement' with ESPN to air a 24-team playoff.
Unanimous approval of 24 teams from 2027-28 through 2031-32. ESPN signs a 5-year ~$1.7B deal for the new games. Power 4 title games are eliminated.

revenueDistribution.basis: Net CFP revenue after participation and expense payments, split by fixed conference percentages. ESPN reports the 24-team deal keeps this distribution unchanged.

shares.notes: Shared by the six G6 leagues. The split among them is not necessarily equal. One outlet cites a 10% G6 share for 2026-27, and another says the G6 got ~25% of base revenue under the old contract. Treat these as unreconciled.
About $12.5M a year, double its old amount, plus a performance bonus. Some reports round to $12M (~1%).

revenueDistribution.previousModel2014to2026: Equal base shares for each Power 5 conference, a smaller pooled share for the Group of Five, fixed payments for Notre Dame and independents, plus academic-performance and participation payments. Under the 2024-26 12-team contract the Pac-12 kept full P5 status through 2025-26.
revenueDistribution.notes: Brief's 29/29/17/15/9 + ND ~$12M is confirmed, more precisely ACC 17.25% and Big 12 14.75%. Per-school estimates come from CBS/Yahoo March 2024 reporting: roughly $21-22M per Big Ten/SEC school and ~$12M per ACC/Big 12 school per year.

seasons2024to2026.notes: Paid to the team's conference, not the school. The travel allowance figure comes from secondary reporting.

season2026_27.note: Assumed to continue the 2024-26 ladder. A 2026-27 schedule was not found.

seasons2027plus.note: Not published. With 23 games and 16 on campus, the per-round amounts are expected to be reworked. Campus hosts keep their home gate.

conferencePassThrough.policy: Schools keep 100% of CFP participation payments. This is the only P4 league that does so.
School keeps $3.0M (first round), $3.5M (quarterfinal), $3.75M (semifinal), $4.0M (title game) plus a travel allowance. The rest is pooled and shared equally.
School keeps at least $1.9M plus travel for each of the first two rounds and $2.2M plus travel for the semifinal and title game. The rest is pooled.

Mostly pooled. Ohio State ($91.6M) and Penn State ($88.9M) topped FY2025 distributions after their CFP runs, so participants do keep a meaningful premium. A fan-forum report claims the participant share rose from ~$5.5M to ~$21M.

base.sublicense: ESPN sublicenses some games to TNT Sports (tnt). TNT has aired first-round and quarterfinal games since 2024-25, and its package was extended to include a semifinal from 2026-27. TNT has 5 games in 2026-27.

expansion.inventory: 12 new games per year: 8 first-round games and 4 added second-round games. All are on campus.
expansion.broadcastCommitments: At least 3 games from each of the new first and second rounds on ABC. ESPN may sublicense up to half of the new inventory (up to 4 first-round and 2 second-round games).
expansion.netOfRebates: ESPN gets back about $140M a year from the SEC, ACC and Big 12 for their canceled title games, so its net new spend is about $205M a year. Fox reportedly gets about $50M a year back from the Big Ten for its title game. Yahoo calls the net gain to conferences 'minimal on a per-school basis', roughly $125M a year shared, much of it replacing lost championship-game gate and sponsorship.
expansion.altFigures: On3 reported more than $320M a year extra, and others reported ~$340M a year.
expansion.note: The headline $1.7B is well sourced. The rebate figures come from single outlets.

previous.notes: The original 4-team contract. ESPN paid more for the added 12-team games in 2024-25 and 2025-26.

managementCommittee.composition: The 10 FBS commissioners plus Notre Dame's athletic director. It runs day-to-day operations and the format, and recommends to the Board of Managers.

boardOfManagers.composition: One president or chancellor for each of the 10 FBS conferences plus Notre Dame's president. It is the CFP's top authority.

votingRules.through2025_26: Substantive changes such as format and revenue needed unanimous approval of the 11-member Board of Managers, on the Management Committee's recommendation.
votingRules.from2026_27: Under the 2024 MOU, the SEC and Big Ten jointly control format decisions. They consult the other conferences, who cannot block. Fixed guarantees: at least 12 teams, automatic access for the ACC and Big 12 champions, at least one G6 bid, and the Notre Dame top-12 guarantee. If the SEC and Big Ten deadlock, the default continues (this happened for 2026). Revenue shares are fixed through 2031-32. Reports said weighted voting would likely replace unanimity on other matters.
votingRules.nov2026Decision: The 24-team decision was reported as unanimous, even though only the SEC and Big Ten's agreement was legally required.
votingRules.note: No MOU text was retrieved. Reconstructed from news summaries.

chair2026.title: Arkansas AD
chair2026.notes: Took over mid-2025 after Mack Rhoades (Baylor) resigned. Returned as chair for 2026.

ny6Bowls.notes: Will not host a semifinal in 2028-31. Keeps its Jan 1 time slot as a quarterfinal.
